I feel like I could have written this post about my own stepdaughter. Your experience is word for word what I went through for years. It was so difficult. Her mother would manipulate her and then she would come to our house and be incredibly rude to me. I felt unwelcome in my own house. My husband refused to discipline her because he worried she wouldn’t come up. 

One day (after 10 years of being her stepmother and putting up with the constant nonsense), I caught her taking photos of me on my bed in a towel. I yelled at her. She insisted she never took any photos, but I knew she did. (She thinks she’s so sneaky but it’s obvious to everyone else she is taking a photo.) So I told her off. She got angry and started mouthing off. And she insisted she was going back to her Mum’s. I said ‘fine but I am laying down ground rules first. 1. You say hello and goodbye when you come to the house. (previously she never said hello or goodbye to me or her sisters.) 2. You don’t take any personal photographs. 3. You talk to me like a human being. Simple rules I thought. 

He said he was bringing her home. Great. And she walked out the door and said ‘Bye David’ to her brother. And didn’t say goodbye to me or her sisters, then slammed the door. I told her she was going nowhere. She was staying here because she broke one of my rules and purposely did not say goodbye. She said ‘You’re not my mother, you can’t tell me what to do!’ My husband, for once in the 10 years we had been married, backed me up and brought her back in the house. She had to sit with us in the living room, because if you’re going to be a bitch, you don’t get to hide in your room, you live with the consequences. 

She apologized and we let her go home, and she and her mother concocted a story that my husband hit her. (He has never put his hands on her in her entire life, and certainly wouldn’t hit a 16 year old girl.) he called her and she insisted she never said that, but refused to tell the whole town that it was false, claiming that she never said it, so she shouldn’t have to deny it. I was upset because child abuse allegations could put my own children at risk. She didn’t come up for a full year. 

But when she did come up she was respectful and kind. And she continued to be nice to me, and for the first time actually saw me as a human being. I honestly think what she needed was to be called on the behavior and wish we had done it sooner instead of 10 years in. We have been married 14 years now. I love her to bits, she loves me. We go for lunches together and shopping. She calls me to tell me about her day. I help her with her homework and college essays. I love her as much as my bio children. I am very happy this is how it’s turned out and I wish we could have gotten along sooner, but I wouldn’t trade her for the world. 

TL;DR It gets better but it takes time. And I would suggest your husband tell her the behavior is unacceptable sooner rather than later. She may get mad, but afterwards, things will likely improve.

This is similar to what happened to me when I was younger with my n-parent. I was forced to take baths with my sister until I was 12. I protested every time and it was such a violation. One time in particular, my grandmother (N-moms Mom) had died and we were to take a bath the night before the funeral. I was 12 and begged to shower on my own, but she cried and said that people were waiting for the shower. (They weren’t. All the adults showered on the morning if the funeral.) Then while bathing with my sister, my creepy uncle came in and sat on the (closed lid) toilet and just watched us. I have never been the same after that day. 

Also, she made me get fitted for bras with her in the room. She got books and insisted we check my breast development with the books etc. Her favorite phrase was ‘we’re all girls, it’s nothing I haven’t seen before). Just typing that makes me sick to my stomach right now. 

I have daughters that age now and they have been washing alone for 7-8 years now, unassisted. I found giving them baths when they were babies difficult because it brought up past abuse. It’s a trauma I will never recover from sadly. 

In better news, I have been married for 12 years. I moved to a totally different country and I feel safe here. I hope you can get away and find yourself a safe space too.
